newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT--Kodak names consumer imaging COOs.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT--Kodak names consumer imaging COOs.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co Wednesday named Henri Petit and Patric Siewert as consumer imaging joint COOs. A full text of the company's press release follows.

ROCHESTER, N.Y.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--June 25, 1997--Eastman Kodak Company today accelerated its efforts to strengthen its global focus and improve the implementation of its worldwide business strategies by announcing a series of key management changes.

The company announced the appointments of Henri D. Petit and Patrick T. Siewert as Chief Operating Officers of Consumer Imaging, Kodak's largest business. Also appointed to new positions are Charles S. Brown, Jr., as Assistant General Manager, Sensitized Goods Manufacturing for the company, and Alexander V. Wasilov, as Chairman and President of Kodak's Greater China Region.

Siewert and Petit will report to David Biehn, President of Consumer Imaging and a Senior Vice President of the company. Brown will report to Richard T. Bourns, Senior Vice President and head of Sensitized Goods Manufacturing. Wasilov will report to Carl F. Kohrt, Assistant Chief Operating Officer, based in Hong Kong.

Both Petit, a French national who currently heads the company's operations in its European, African and Middle Eastern Region, and Siewert, Chairman of the company's Greater China Region, have extensive operational experience outside the U.S. Petit, a technologist trained in electronics and nuclear physics, has held a number of general management positions both in Europe and on a worldwide basis. Siewert, who started his career in sales and marketing, has spent most of his 23-year Kodak career with responsibilities outside the U.S. His general management experience spans the consumer, professional, and graphics businesses.

"Petit and Siewert have excellent track records in driving results in the face of challenging business opportunities," said Daniel A. Carp, Kodak President and Chief Operating Officer. "Siewert's career responsibilities have taken him from the U.S. and Canada, to Europe and now China. He brings a unique global perspective to his new role. Petit combines his own international credentials with a record of business success. He understands traditional photography and digital imaging both as a technologist and general manager."

Wasilov, currently Chief Operating Officer, Consumer Imaging, and Vice President, replaces Siewert as head of the Greater China Region. Prior to becoming head of Kodak's Consumer Imaging operations in the U.S. and Canada in 1994, Wasilov managed the company's Consumer business in Japan. His experience in managing Kodak's single largest business will be a substantial asset as Kodak works to develop China into a world-class participant in the global photographic industry.

Brown, a technologist with extensive manufacturing and product development experience, is currently Chief Operating Officer, Consumer Imaging, and Vice President, and becomes Assistant General Manager of worldwide sensitized goods manufacturing. He and Bourns will share leadership of the company's global manufacturing facilities, responsible for producing photographic film and papers for all Kodak businesses.

"Wasilov and Brown have made significant contributions to Kodak's Consumer business, during a period in which we gained worldwide share and launched the best family of color films in the world," said David P. Biehn, President of Consumer Imaging, and a Senior Vice President of Kodak. "Their new assignments will take advantage of their individual talents while allowing them to grow as senior leaders."

Biehn also noted that Brown's new assignment will allow him to apply his business skills to a manufacturing role while Wasilov will significantly broaden his scope of leadership beyond consumer imaging to the company's entire business portfolio and manufacturing operations in China.

Carp added that as Kodak continues to focus its operations through worldwide business units, the company must accelerate the pace of change. "In this regard, it is vital that we develop leaders with strong global business savvy in a more rapid manner," he said. "This series of moves allows a number of key executives to further their development as global business executives."

Petit, 49, joined Kodak's French subsidiary, Kodak Pathe, in 1975 in the manufacturing organization. He subsequently served in a variety of management positions in Europe in Business Imaging Systems, Photofinishing, and Motion Picture & Television Imaging. He was elected a company vice president in 1992 and ran the Motion Picture & Television business on a worldwide basis through 1995. He returned to Europe in his current role that same year. Petit holds a M.S. in engineering from Ecole Superieure de Physique et Chimie de Paris, a post-graduate degree in nuclear physics and a Ph.D. in corpuscular electronics from the University of Paris XI, France. He also attended the Advanced Management Program, I.N.S.E.A.D., Fontainbleau, France.

Siewert, 41, joined Kodak in 1974. He worked in both Chicago and Rochester in a variety of assignments in the Consumer, Professional and Photofinishing businesses. He was assistant to the President and General Manager of Kodak Canada in 1986; and in 1987, he was appointed Director of Worldwide Business and Product Planning for Professional Imaging, before moving to London in 1990 as Director of Business Planning and Finance for the company's International Group. In 1992 he was named Regional Business General Manager for Professional and Printing Imaging, Europe, Africa and Middle Eastern Region.

Siewert was named Deputy Chairman of the company's Greater China Region in 1994, becoming Chairman in January 1997. He was elected a company vice president in 1995. Siewert studied photography at Rochester Institute of Technology and was graduated from Elmhurst College, Elmhurst, Ill, where he received a B.S. in Business Administration.

Wasilov, 43, joined Kodak in 1975, holding a variety of sales and marketing positions prior to being named Regional Business Manager for Consumer Imaging in Japan in 1988. He was named General Manager and Vice President of U.S. Marketing in Consumer Imaging in 1991. He was elected a corporate vice president and named Regional General Manager of the U.S. and Canada Region of Consumer Imaging in 1994. He became Chief Operating Officer of Consumer Imaging worldwide in 1995. In addition to managing the five geographic regions, Wasilov was also responsible for managing Kodak's worldwide Consumer Imaging services business (photofinishing). Wasilov graduated from Pennsylvania State University with a BS, and the University of Rhode Island with a MBA.

Brown, 47, joined Kodak in 1973 as a chemical engineer in the Synthetic Chemicals Division. He has held a variety of management positions in manufacturing, product, and process development. He was graduated from Cornell University with both a B.S. and M.ENG. in Chemical Engineering. He holds an M.S. in Management from MIT's Sloan School and an MBA from RIT. He was named Chief Operating Officer of Consumer Imaging and elected a corporate vice president in 1995. In this capacity, he was responsible for product businesses and linkages with the company's manufacturing and R&D operations.

In a related announcement, John Tseng, a Chinese national, was appointed regional business general manager, Consumer Imaging, and vice president Greater China Region, reporting to Siewert and Wasilov in that capacity.

Tseng, 47, joined Kodak in 1982 as an assistant marketing manager in Taiwan. He has held a variety of sales, marketing, and product management positions in Taiwan, China, and Rochester. Tseng was graduated from Soochow University, Taipei, Taiwan, with a BA and the American Graduate School of International Management, Arizona, with a Master's in International Management.
The appointments are effective Sept. 1, 1997. -0- Editor's Note: For additional information about Kodak, visit our web site on the Internet at: http://www.kodak.com/
